President Obama prescribed an order of succession under which the 
commissioner of CBP would be the seventh in line. Exec. Order 13,753, 81 
Fed. Reg. 90667 (2016). The Obama order revised a 2003 executive order 
issued by President Bush, with a somewhat different order. Exec. Order 
No. 13,286, 68 Fed. Reg. 10619 (2003). Two weeks after the Obama order, 
however. Congress amended the Homeland Security Act to eliminate the 
FVRA as a source of presidential authority to determine the DHS order of 
succession. National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017, Pub. 
L. 114-328, § 1903(a)(2), 130 Stat. 2000, 2672 (2016), adding 6 U.S.C.
§ 113(g). Authority to establish an order of succession now rests with the 
Secretary. As of the day on which Kevin McAleenan was announced as 
Acting Secretary, no such order had been pubhshed.
President Trump made clear what he took to be the advantages of 
acting officers. He said in a television interview, ‘T like ‘acting’ because I 
can move so quickly. It gives me more flexibility.”
For bis part. President Biden used agency-specific statutory authority 
to prevent a defeat in the Senate from denying him his choice of a cabinet 
secretary. Biden appointed—and the Senate confirmed—Julie Su to be 
Deputy Secretary of Labor shortly after Biden took office in 2021. In March 
2023, when Labor Secretary Martin Walsh resigned, Biden promptly 
nominated Su to be his successor. Unfortunately for Su, a couple of shaky 
votes within the Democrats’ bare Senate majority made it unlikely she 
would be confirmftd. Hence, Democratic Senate Majority Leader Chuck 
Schumer of New York then dehberately kept Su’s nomination off the 
Senate’s calendar, effectively letting it pend indefinitely.
As it happens, the Labor Department’s organic act states: “[t]he 
Deputy Secretary shall ... in case of the death, resignation, or removal 
from office of the Secretary, perform the duties of the Secretary until a 
successor is appointed.” The President was able to install Su as the acting 
secretary, citing the authority of this statute, which has no time limit. But 
Biden could also have cited the FVRA in support. The FVRA ordinarily 
limits a vacancy appointment to 210 days after the vacancy occurred (or if 
it occurred during a Senate recess, to 210 days after the Senate 
reconvenes). But there are exceptions. First, the FVRA offers an explicit 
exemption when another statute, like the Labor Department’s, temporarily 
“designates an officer or employee to perform the functions and duties of a 
specified office.” 5 U.S.C. § 3347(a)(1)(B). Moreover, the 210-day limit is 
superseded “once a first or second nomination for the office is submitted to 
the Senate,” 5 U.S.C. § 3346(a) (2), as long as the nomination is pending. 
Given the Schumer gambit of never bringing Su’s confirmation vote 
forward, her nomination was assured to be pending for the duration of the 
Biden Administration.
